the merge or the check run being observed, the health state changing — and by a backstop poll
(default every 5 minutes; the legacy poll is 30). A resolved cause returns the item to the queue
with a notice. An `infra` cause returns an item at most twice (default). A `defect` cause naming
no existing task files one.
acceptance: AC1: The CPV2-606/607/608 case is a scenario: three items parked on one defect return when the defect's fix merges, with no poll involved.
AC2: An item with no cause, a `decision` cause or an unknown kind is never auto-returned.
AC3: Workers can name a cause in their account; the packet asks for it; the self-heal agent or a person can set one.

AC4: Demonstration (parity, MS5) — the recorded parked items and their causes are replayed, timing from the resolving event to the item being back in the queue. Target: back within 60 s for every cause Sortyard observes itself. Floor: back within 5 minutes; the legacy poll is at most every 30 minutes (BL-06).
requirements.source: conductor README "Blocking causes" (`causes.py`, `POLL`, `RETURNS`; Joe 2026-11-06).
requirements.baseline: `causes.tick` polls each parked item at most every 30 minutes, a limit set by the board's rate limit, so resolved work waits up to that long to return (conductor README "Blocking causes"; BL-06).

measured.target: back within 60 s for every cause Sortyard observes itself.
measured.floor: back within 5 minutes; the legacy poll is at most every 30 minutes (BL-06).

requirements.title: The self-heal contract
requirements.statement:
The self-heal queue is worked by an agent or person with access workers lack. Each item ends in
one recorded outcome: **fixed directly** (with verification), **outcome already met** (RDY-008),
**handed back to build** (diagnosis and exact change written at the top of the task), **moot**
(evidence, then Cancelled), or **owner input** (converted to or linked with a decision). Self-heal
principals never merge, approve or review, and never add merge gates.
acceptance: AC1: The resolution action requires one of the five outcomes and its evidence field.
AC2: The self-heal role's token cannot call review or merge operations (authorization matrix test).
AC3: The list of projects to scan comes from the same configuration the scheduler uses; there is no second list.
requirements.source: conductor `SELF-HEAL.md`; HARNESS-248 (the contract listed the wrong project identifier).

requirements.title: Self-heal drain
requirements.statement:
While any task of a project has been in self-heal or `needs_human` for longer than the drain
limit (default 24 hours, the legacy value), one urgent `SELF-HEAL-STALLED <project>` condition
lists each item, its stop reason and its age. It closes only when nothing of the project remains
in either queue.
acceptance: AC1: The condition is updated in place and never duplicated.
requirements.source: conductor README "Self-heal drain" (35 open self-heal items, 21 untouched for 24 h; HARNESS-444).

requirements.title: Phase and age are always visible
requirements.statement:
Every in-flight chain's phase, slot use and time in phase are visible through API, CLI and UI. A
chain in one phase longer than the stall threshold (default 4 h) gets exactly one notice saying
where it is stuck.
acceptance: AC1: The information the legacy conductor kept only in `state.json` (phase, slot use, stale live records, running revision) is readable without cluster access.

AC2: Demonstration (count, MS3) — the facts an operator needs about work in flight (phase, slot use, time in phase, stale records, running revision) are listed with where each is read. Target: 100% through the API, the CLI and the console, each within 1 s. Floor: none needs cluster access; in the legacy system every one of them does (BL-28).
requirements.source: driver §4 "Visibility"; task-pickup conformance row 7 (HARNESS-256).
requirements.baseline: Phase, slot use, stale live records and the running revision are readable only in `state.json` on a cluster volume or as a cluster annotation (task-pickup conformance row 7, HARNESS-256; BL-28).

measured.target: 100% through the API, the CLI and the console, each within 1 s.
measured.floor: none needs cluster access; in the legacy system every one of them does (BL-28).

requirements.title: Side effects are idempotent and recorded when accepted
requirements.statement:
Each external write (a Job, a push, a change request, a comment, an auto-merge toggle) is
recorded only once the external system accepted it, so a failure is retried on the next
reconcile; and each has an idempotency marker, so a retry after a lost response does not repeat
it.
acceptance: AC1: Lose the response to each kind of write in turn: the effect exists exactly once afterwards (fault-injection matrix).
AC2: A notice of a given kind for a given condition is posted once.
requirements.source: `drive.py` notes 242, 250, 416, 422 ("persisted first: a partial GitHub failure cannot loop the toggle").

requirements.title: Idempotent submission
requirements.statement:
Creating operations accept an idempotency key: the same key with the same payload returns the
original result; the same key with a different payload is refused.
acceptance: AC1: A retried create after a lost response creates one object.
AC2: Internally, a refusal for key reuse makes the next attempt use a fresh key rather than retrying the same one forever.
requirements.source: driver §5 (`client_request_id` is idempotent); driver "Recovery" (409 advances the attempt counter).

requirements.title: Controller restart and failover
requirements.statement:
At most one controller acts at a time (leader election with a fencing epoch). After a crash,
restart or failover a new leader resumes with no duplicate Jobs, change requests, comments or
merges and no lost stage result. A leader that is shutting down hands over instead of letting
its lease lapse.
acceptance: AC1: Chaos test: kill the leader at random points during 200 chains; the end state equals a run with no kills.
AC2: A deposed leader's writes are refused by the epoch check.

AC3: Demonstration (chaos, MS3) — the leader is killed at random points during 200 chains, timing from the kill to the next reconcile by a leader. Target: at most 15 s, with an end state equal to a run with no kills. Floor: at most 60 s; the legacy system resumes at its next pass, up to three minutes later (BL-25).
requirements.source: inference from the single-writer constraints today (`concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` on the CronJobs; `strategy: Recreate` "single writer to the sqlite db: never two pods").
requirements.baseline: One writer is guaranteed by `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` on the CronJobs and `strategy: Recreate` on the API; work interrupted by a crash is picked up at the next pass, and every rollout has 30 to 40 seconds with nothing listening (task-pickup §3; `k8s/deployment.yaml`; BL-25).

measured.target: at most 15 s, with an end state equal to a run with no kills.
measured.floor: at most 60 s; the legacy system resumes at its next pass, up to three minutes later (BL-25).

requirements.title: Version skew never pauses delivery silently
requirements.statement:
Adjacent versions run side by side: the controller and the API of one minor version work with
the schema and the stage contract of the previous one (DEP-007, DEP-009), so an upgrade does not
pause delivery. Only a schema outside that window makes the controller idle: it writes nothing
and reports `skew` in health at once (`/readyz`, `/v1/info`, the Overview); from MS5 its missed
heartbeats also raise a `SILENT` condition (REC-017).
acceptance: AC1: During a rolling upgrade between adjacent minors no reconcile is skipped for skew, and no reconcile ever runs against a schema outside the supported window.
AC2: The skew state is visible wherever health is shown; it is never a silent idle.

AC3: Demonstration (chaos, MS3) — a rolling upgrade runs during 20 chains, and separately an upgrade is made to stall half-way, measuring the seconds in which no reconcile runs and the time until the stall is reported. Target: zero paused seconds, and a stuck upgrade reported within 60 s. Floor: paused at most 60 s and never silently; the legacy system skipped every pass for about 32 minutes with only a log line (BL-08, BL-25).
requirements.source: conductor README "API rollouts" (`api_skew`; "ends without touching `state.json`"); 2026-11-12 release stall ("pass skipped, rollout: API bundle …" for about 32 min with no visible alarm).
requirements.baseline: On version skew the legacy pass ends without writing. On 2026-11-12 every pass was skipped for about 32 minutes while the API pod held an old bundle, with no alarm (conductor README "API rollouts"; BL-08, BL-25).

measured.target: zero paused seconds, and a stuck upgrade reported within 60 s.
measured.floor: paused at most 60 s and never silently; the legacy system skipped every pass for about 32 minutes with only a log line (BL-08, BL-25).

requirements.title: Dependency outages are waited out
requirements.statement:
Connection-level failures to the database, the API, the Git host or the cluster API are retried
with capped backoff (default schedule, the legacy one: 1, 2, 4, 8, 15 s up to 90 s). A reconcile
that cannot proceed ends without partial writes. No verdict, review outcome or grooming result
is recorded as `failed` or `unavailable` because a dependency was briefly down.
acceptance: AC1: Eleven simulated 40-second restarts in a day produce zero failed reviews and zero parked items.
requirements.source: conductor README "API rollouts" (11 rollouts failed grooming, flake processing and test reviews with ECONNREFUSED).

requirements.title: Every recurring mechanism has a freshness window
requirements.statement:
Every loop and scheduled job inside Sortyard is registered with an owner route, a cadence and a
freshness window no shorter than the cadence. One that goes quiet past its window raises one
`SILENT <mechanism>` condition carrying last success, last error, cadence and window, and closes
it when heartbeats resume. The checker runs independently of everything it watches and is itself
registered.
acceptance: AC1: Stopping any registered loop produces its `SILENT` condition inside its window (one test per mechanism, generated from the registry).
AC2: Adding a loop without registering it fails CI (registry coverage test).
AC3: With the scheduler and the integrator both down, the checker still reports them.
requirements.source: MECHANISMS.md (registry, `conductor-mechanism-health` runs apart from drive and plane-sync; fixtures 1–9); k3s-harness #321.

requirements.title: External heartbeats
requirements.statement:
Jobs outside Sortyard can register as mechanisms and post heartbeats
(`{mechanism, status, error?, at?}`) with a token. An unknown name raises `UNREGISTERED <name>`.
A heartbeat that cannot be delivered is noticed by its absence.
acceptance: AC1: The heartbeat client is one HTTP call and never fails the job it wraps.
AC2: Cluster-object and CI-workflow observers (CronJob last success, resource conditions, scheduled workflow runs) are an optional integration, required before legacy retirement (MIG-012).
requirements.source: MECHANISMS.md "Heartbeats from jump-box and Juno-side jobs", heartbeat kinds `cronjob`, `resource`, `workflow`, `pr-runs`.

requirements.title: Health has four states and never hides the unknown
requirements.statement:
Overall health is the worst of: `silent-check` (the checker's own report is stale), `degraded`
(any silent mechanism, low quota, missing reading or unregistered mechanism), `partial` (some
sources unreadable), `healthy`. A source that cannot be read makes its mechanisms `unknown`: not
filed, not closed, named in the report.
acceptance: AC1: An unreadable source never yields `healthy`.
AC2: `/readyz` and the Overview show the state and what is driving it.
requirements.source: MECHANISMS.md "FACTORY-HEALTH-SENSOR input".

requirements.title: One writer per chain, enforced at the side-effect boundary
requirements.statement:
A chain has a revision (epoch) that increases on claim, on requeue, on cancel and on an
operator's steering change. Every side-effecting operation carries the epoch it was planned
under and is refused when it is stale: stage result submission, pushes, change-request writes,
merges.
acceptance: AC1: A worker from a cancelled or superseded attempt submits a result: it is refused and recorded as stale.
AC2: The check is in the integrator and the API, not only in the controller's memory.

AC3: Demonstration (chaos, MS3) — superseded workers, deposed controllers and cancelled attempts each try every side effect (result, push, change-request write, merge) 1,000 times. Target: 100% refused at the integrator or the API and recorded as stale. Floor: zero stale side effects accepted; the legacy system has no check at that boundary (BL-28).
requirements.source: in-flight-steering ("A durable per-task revision must eventually be checked by the actual side-effecting execution boundary … Until that path is implemented … report its absence honestly").
requirements.baseline: No durable per-task revision is checked where side effects happen; the steering document says to report that absence honestly (in-flight-steering; BL-28).

measured.target: 100% refused at the integrator or the API and recorded as stale.
measured.floor: zero stale side effects accepted; the legacy system has no check at that boundary (BL-28).

requirements.title: Steering work in flight
requirements.statement:
An operator can change a task that is already in flight: edit its text (the next stage reads the
new text and stale findings are dropped), cancel the running stage, or stop the chain. Steering
revises the existing chain; it never starts a competing one.
acceptance: AC1: After a mid-flight edit there is still exactly one chain for the task, with a higher epoch.
AC2: Evidence that the change did not invalidate is reused; only invalidated reviews re-run.

AC3: Demonstration (benchmark, MS4) — a scripted operator edits a task's text mid-build, cancels a stage and stops a chain, counting steps and the reviews that re-run. Target: one action each, in force at the next stage, with only invalidated reviews re-run. Floor: each is done from the console with no cluster access and no competing chain; the legacy procedure is manual (BL-28).
requirements.source: in-flight-steering ("steering revises the existing task"); driver §7 ("Stop an item mid-flight: Not supported yet").
requirements.baseline: Stopping or steering an item in flight is a prose procedure, and stopping one mid-flight is "Not supported yet" (driver §7; in-flight-steering; BL-28).

measured.target: one action each, in force at the next stage, with only invalidated reviews re-run.
measured.floor: each is done from the console with no cluster access and no competing chain; the legacy procedure is manual (BL-28).

requirements.title: Work storage is cleaned under pressure, never under a live chain
requirements.statement:
Finished run directories are kept for a retention time (default 24 h). At or above a usage
threshold (default 85%) retention drops (default 4 h) with no per-pass cap. A directory any live
chain still needs is never deleted. Deletion runs detached so dispatch never waits on it.
acceptance: AC1: Filling the volume in a test triggers pressure retention and dispatch latency is unaffected.
AC2: Volume usage is a metric with a warning threshold (OBS-010) and, from MS5, an attention item (OBS-014), before it is an outage.
requirements.source: driver §5 (`MH_WORK_PRESSURE_PCT`, `MH_WORK_RETENTION_PRESSURE_S`; k3s-harness #187, #189); `mh.py` retention (notes).

requirements.title: Conditions: one alarm per cause, updated in place, closed by the system
requirements.statement:
System-raised alarms are `condition` tasks with a stable key. A condition is created once per
cause, updated in place while the cause persists, never duplicated — even after losing every
cache — and closed with a notice when the cause clears. The v1 conditions: `FILING-INVISIBLE`,
`CONFIG-INVALID`, `GROOMING-STALLED`, `SELF-HEAL-STALLED`, `SILENT`, `QUOTA`, `UNREGISTERED`,
`CITATION-MISMATCH`, `RELEASE-VERIFY-FAILED`.
acceptance: AC1: Raising the same cause 100 times yields one open task.
AC2: Each condition names an owner route and appears in that route's list.
requirements.source: conductor README (each of these items is described as "updated in place, never duplicated, and closed when…"); MECHANISMS.md.

requirements.title: The owner is never a step inside delivery
requirements.statement:
No workflow blocks on a person. People are reached only through decisions (with defaults),
needs routed to them, and escalations. The owner list contains exactly: open decisions due,
premise-class decisions escalated, needs routed to `owner`, and items escalated "to a person".
acceptance: AC1: The owner list is one API call; an item appears on it for one of the four reasons, shown.
AC2: A notification reaches the owner only for an owner-list item or a factory-down state with nothing acting on it (OBS-013).

AC3: Operator actions on work in flight (requeue, cancel, force, manual state change, resolving a hand-back), counted from the ledger for each week and for each 100 merged tasks (`operator.interventions`). Target: zero in a week. Floor: fewer for each 100 merged tasks than the legacy baseline (BL-07).
requirements.source: driver §6 ("The owner is never a step inside delivery"; "Slack is only for what the owner alone can do, or the factory being down with nothing acting on it").

measured.target: zero in a week.
measured.floor: fewer for each 100 merged tasks than the legacy baseline (BL-07).

requirements.title: Parity and chaos suites
requirements.statement:
Two suites gate the milestone that makes Sortyard safe to leave alone: a **parity suite** with at
least one scenario for every KEEP or FIX row of [16-legacy-parity.md](16-legacy-parity.md) whose
requirements are MUST and due by MS5, run against the Git host and CI fakes (rows owed by a
SHOULD or by a later milestone gain their scenario with that requirement and are complete
before the estate's cutovers, MIG-010); and a **chaos suite** that injects controller kills, worker
pod loss, database restarts, Git host errors, model-capacity errors, a stale mirror and a full
work volume.
acceptance: AC1: The parity matrix is machine-readable: CI fails when a row that is due has no passing scenario, and reports every other row as pending with the milestone that owes it.
AC2: After each chaos run, every task is in a terminal or owned state and no slot is held past its bound.
AC3: A scenario that is a demonstration runs with its legacy baseline beside it, writes the measured value to the scorecard (QLT-051) and fails below its floor.
requirements.source: inference — the legacy system encodes its behaviour in `test_conductor.py` (10,364 lines) and `test_mh.py` (3,268 lines); a claims-only shadow comparison cannot exercise the step machine.

requirements.title: Stalls are detected and recovered in minutes
requirements.statement:
A stall is found by the system, not by a watch or a person, and is recovered or owned within
minutes. Three mechanisms. (1) Each phase's bound is derived from that phase's own history (a
multiple of its recent p95, policy data) instead of one flat threshold, with the legacy stall
threshold as the ceiling. (2) A no-progress watchdog: a stage that produces no output,
heartbeat or state change for `stage.no_progress_seconds` (default 600) is ended and retried or
parked under its failure budget. (3) A task in self-heal that nothing has picked up within
`selfheal.unpicked_seconds` (default 900) is put on the attention list and sent to its route.
Every stall class in the catalogue has a named recovery, and every episode is recorded
(`stall.episodes`) with its detection and recovery times.
acceptance: AC1: Demonstration (chaos, MS5) — every stall class of the baseline catalogue (BL-05) is injected during the 72-hour run and the recorded episodes are replayed. Target: 100% of catalogued classes have a recovery, at least 95% of episodes heal with no person, detection within 60 s and recovery within 10 minutes at p95. Floor: a higher self-healed share and a lower median time to recovery than the legacy baselines (BL-05, BL-06).
AC2: A bound derived from history is never longer than the ceiling, and a phase with too little history uses the ceiling (default: the legacy stall threshold).
AC3: Each recovery names the watch or alert it retires, in the migration guide (MIG-011); no new watch is added for a stall class that has a recovery.
requirements.source: conductor README "Self-heal drain" and "Incident notes"; task-pickup §5; the estate's practice of building a recovery for each stall class instead of another watch. The three mechanisms are inference from the recorded episodes.
requirements.baseline: One flat stall threshold of 4 hours; parked causes polled at most every 30 minutes; 35 self-heal items open with 21 untouched for 24 hours (HARNESS-444); recorded episodes of 8, 9 and 20 hours and of two days (BL-05, BL-06).

measured.target: 100% of catalogued classes have a recovery, at least 95% of episodes heal with no person, detection within 60 s and recovery within 10 minutes at p95.
measured.floor: a higher self-healed share and a lower median time to recovery than the legacy baselines (BL-05, BL-06).

requirements.title: One versioned REST API with a served OpenAPI document
requirements.statement:
The API lives under `/v1`, is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 document served at
`/v1/openapi.json`, and CI fails if the implementation and the document disagree. Resource shapes
come from the JSON Schemas in `spec/`, from which the Python models are generated.
acceptance: AC1: A contract test calls every operation in the document against a running server and validates each response against its schema.
AC2: `python -m sortyard.models.codegen --check` and the OpenAPI drift check gate every PR; the `spec` job is no longer `continue-on-error`.

AC3: Surface parity, measured at every merge to `main`: the share of the commands a person or an agent may perform that are REST operations, and the share of REST operations that have a CLI path, MCP reach and, when operator-facing, a console control. Target: 100% on all four at every merge, with no exemption. Floor: 100% for REST, CLI and MCP at every merge; console exemptions are dated and empty at each milestone exit (UI-002).
requirements.source: spec NOTES "API conventions"; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `spec` job currently fails on main and does not gate); goldfish GF1-02, GF1-09.

measured.target: 100% on all four at every merge, with no exemption.
measured.floor: 100% for REST, CLI and MCP at every merge; console exemptions are dated and empty at each milestone exit (UI-002).

requirements.title: Commands live in the domain layer; the API adds no rules
requirements.statement:
State machines, invariants and ledger writes are enforced in the domain layer (and by database
constraints where possible). HTTP handlers authenticate, authorise, validate shape and call a
command.
acceptance: AC1: The same command called from an HTTP handler and called in-process (the controller's path) produces identical state and events (shared test).
AC2: No invariant test depends on going through HTTP.

AC3: Demonstration (chaos, MS3) — the API is stopped for 10 minutes while chains are in flight. Target: claims, the advancement of finished stages and landing continue throughout, every result produced meanwhile is accepted when the API returns, and zero stages fail. Floor: no evaluation is skipped and no stage fails because the API is down; the legacy conductor skipped every pass while its API was unavailable (BL-25).
requirements.source: DESIGN §4 ("API service — the only door"); see CF-07 for why the controller does not use HTTP.
requirements.baseline: The legacy conductor is a client of the dispatcher's API. On 2026-11-12 every drive pass was skipped for about 32 minutes while the API pod held an old bundle, and API rollouts have failed reviews, grooming and flake processing (conductor README "API rollouts"; BL-25, BL-08).

measured.target: claims, the advancement of finished stages and landing continue throughout, every result produced meanwhile is accepted when the API returns, and zero stages fail.
measured.floor: no evaluation is skipped and no stage fails because the API is down; the legacy conductor skipped every pass while its API was unavailable (BL-25).

requirements.title: Conventions
requirements.statement:
Lists use opaque cursors in both directions with `limit` (default 50, max 200), filters and sort
as query parameters, and return a total where it is cheap. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details
with a stable `code`. Status codes: 400 malformed, 401, 403, 404, 409 refused by a state machine
or policy, 412 stale precondition, 422 fails schema validation, 429, 503 dependency unavailable.
Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC; durations are integer seconds.
acceptance: AC1: Every list endpoint passes a shared pagination conformance test (stable order under concurrent inserts, no duplicates or gaps across pages).
AC2: Every error body validates against the problem schema, for every method on every path.
requirements.source: spec NOTES "API conventions"; harness-console J2 ("server cursors in both directions"), decided D6; goldfish GF1-06 (HTML 501 page).

requirements.title: Optimistic concurrency
requirements.statement:
Every mutable object has a revision returned as an `ETag`. `PATCH` and action endpoints accept
`If-Match`; a stale revision returns 412. The console always sends it.
acceptance: AC1: Two clients editing the same task: the second write fails with 412 and loses nothing.
AC2: In-process callers (the controller's path) pass through the same revision check.
requirements.source: inference — the frozen API replaces whole documents by merge patch with no precondition, while the operator, agents and the controller all write tasks; Plane writes of a pod on old code overwrote three specs during the 2026-11-08 import.

requirements.title: Idempotency keys
requirements.statement:
`POST` operations that create or trigger accept an `Idempotency-Key` header with the semantics
of REC-013; keys are remembered for the retention period (default 24 hours).
acceptance: AC1: Contract test: replaying each creating operation with the same key returns the first response.
requirements.source: driver §5 (`client_request_id`).

requirements.title: State changes are named actions
requirements.statement:
`PATCH` edits fields and never changes state or queue status. Each transition is its own
endpoint (`POST …/tasks/{id}/release`, `/requeue`, `/cancel`, `/hand-back/resolve`,
`/decisions/{id}/answer`, …) with its own roles and its required reason fields.
acceptance: AC1: A `PATCH` containing `state` is rejected with 422 naming the action to use.
requirements.source: spec NOTES "API conventions".

requirements.title: Server-assigned ids, client-supplied external ids
requirements.statement:
The server assigns ids and sequence numbers. A client may supply an `external_id` unique within
a project, which makes creates idempotent and lets a file be re-applied.
acceptance: AC1: Creating two tasks with the same `external_id` in one project yields one task.
AC2: No operation requires the client to invent a primary key.
requirements.source: spec NOTES API ambiguity 10 ("`POST` takes the whole object with a client-chosen `id`") — a gap in the frozen spec, not in the estate: Plane assigns ids and sequence numbers today, and `plane_tasks.py file` re-applies a file by task id.

requirements.title: Event stream
requirements.statement:
`GET /v1/…/events/stream` is a server-sent-event stream of ledger events, resumable with
`Last-Event-ID` (the ledger sequence), filterable by project, object and kind. Events are also
listable by cursor.
acceptance: AC1: A client that disconnects and resumes misses nothing and sees nothing twice.
AC2: The stream carries only fields the caller may read.
requirements.source: harness-console decided D5 (SSE keyed by a monotonic id, polling fallback); spec NOTES API ambiguity 15.

requirements.title: Outbound webhooks
requirements.statement:
An operator can register webhook endpoints for event kinds. Deliveries are signed (HMAC-SHA256
over the body with a per-endpoint secret, timestamped), retried with backoff, and logged with
their outcome. Destinations are checked against private, loopback and link-local ranges unless
explicitly allowed.
acceptance: AC1: A receiver can verify signature and timestamp from the documentation alone.
AC2: A webhook pointed at a metadata address or a cluster-internal service is refused by default.
requirements.source: DESIGN §7 ("Webhooks/events out"); Plane benchmark (signed webhooks; nine SSRF advisories — see [12-quality-bar.md](12-quality-bar.md)).

requirements.title: Rate limiting
requirements.statement:
Requests are rate-limited per token and per session; over-limit requests get 429 with
`Retry-After`. Limits are configuration.
acceptance: AC1: Default limits never throttle the bundled console or CLI in the scenario suite.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (API key limit default 60/minute); conductor `causes.tick` polls each parked item at most every 30 minutes "for Plane's rate limit".

requirements.title: Bounded responses and an explicit redaction contract
requirements.statement:
No endpoint returns an unbounded collection. Overview and list responses are built from field
allowlists and never include packets, prompts, check commands, free-form worker facts, tokens or
secrets. Detail endpoints that expose sensitive material (a packet, a trace) are separate
operations with their own role.
acceptance: AC1: A test enumerates every list and overview schema and asserts none references a sensitive field.
AC2: Response size for any list call is bounded independently of history size.
requirements.source: FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN "Decision and boundary" and "Source model and invariants"; harness-console decided D10.

requirements.title: Unknown is not zero
requirements.statement:
Every aggregate carries `as_of` and a coverage state. A value whose source is unread, stale or
incomplete is `null` with a `reason`; a ratio with a zero denominator is `null` with
`no_eligible_items`, never a number.
acceptance: AC1: Shared helper and a lint: aggregate fields are typed as `value | null + reason`.
AC2: The UI renders `unknown` for null (UI-024).
requirements.source: FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN ("They must not be rendered as zero while unconnected"); harness-console J1; factory-measurement-contract "Sources, windows, and missingness".

requirements.title: Stability and deprecation
requirements.statement:
At 1.0 the `/v1` API is frozen: only additive changes within the major. A deprecation is
announced in the changelog and by a `Deprecation` header and stays for at least two minor
releases or six months, whichever is longer. CI checks every PR for breaking changes against the
last released OpenAPI document.
acceptance: AC1: A PR that removes a field or tightens a type fails the compatibility job.
AC2: Before 1.0, each minor's breaking changes are listed in its upgrade notes.
requirements.source: CORPUS M6.3 ("API backward-compatibility checks against the published OpenAPI"); Plane benchmark (no written deprecation policy found in the repo).

requirements.title: Health and identity endpoints
requirements.statement:
`/healthz` is liveness. `/readyz` is ready only when the service can authenticate to the
database and the schema version is the one it expects. `/v1/info` returns version, source
commit, image digest, schema version and the health state (REC-019).
acceptance: AC1: With a wrong database password `/readyz` returns 503 and the rollout does not go green.
AC2: The running revision is visible without cluster access.

AC3: Demonstration (count, MS1) — the facts that answer "what is running, and is it healthy" (version, commit, image digest, schema version, health state) are listed with where each is read. Target: 100% from `/v1/info` in one call. Floor: none needs cluster access; the legacy revision is a cluster annotation (BL-28).
requirements.source: goldfish GF1-07 ("a wrong password installs green"); task-pickup conformance row 7 (running revision visible only as a cluster annotation, HARNESS-256).
requirements.baseline: The running revision is visible only as a cluster annotation (task-pickup conformance row 7, HARNESS-256; BL-28).

measured.target: 100% from `/v1/info` in one call.
measured.floor: none needs cluster access; the legacy revision is a cluster annotation (BL-28).

requirements.title: Bulk filing
requirements.statement:
One operation files a set of tasks with their relations atomically (TRK-012) and returns a
verdict per task.
acceptance: AC1: Filing 200 tasks with dependencies in one call on the reference install. Target: under 1 s. Floor: under 5 s.
requirements.source: `plane_tasks.py file`; the 2026-11-08 import (40 new items, 252 relations).

measured.target: under 1 s.
measured.floor: under 5 s.

requirements.title: Inbound Git host webhooks are an accelerator, not a dependency
requirements.statement:
Sortyard works by polling the Git host. If inbound webhooks are configured, they only shorten
the time to observe a fact; every fact is still confirmed by reading it. Webhook payloads are
verified by signature.
acceptance: AC1: The full scenario suite passes with webhooks disabled.
AC2: A forged webhook changes nothing.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "The rule" (observed state); the estate today polls (`drive` every 3 min, `plane_sync` every 5 min) and cannot receive webhooks on a tailnet-only host.

requirements.title: No controller-only public operations
requirements.statement:
Claiming a task, advancing a chain, instructing the integrator and applying a decision default
are not API operations. The frozen spec's `claimTask`, `advanceTask`, `handBackTask` and
`instructIntegrator` are removed.
acceptance: AC1: The OpenAPI document contains no operation whose only permitted role is the controller.
AC2: System actors (`system:controller`, `system:integrator`, each with its version) are a separate actor type in the ledger, and no API credential can act as one.
requirements.source: PERMISSIONS.md matrix (conductor-only rows); CF-07. The estate has no public claim operation either: the conductor claims inside its own process.

requirements.title: Workspace addressing
requirements.statement:
Every object carries `workspace_id`. Paths are `/v1/workspaces/{workspace}/…`; a single-workspace
installation may address its workspace as `default`.
acceptance: AC1: A 1.0 installation has exactly one workspace; creating a second is refused with a message that multi-workspace isolation is not supported yet.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.1 (the field exists from day one; multi-workspace is a v1 non-goal).

requirements.title: MCP over HTTP from the API service, plus a stdio shim
requirements.statement:
The API service serves MCP over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, authenticated by the same tokens as
REST. `sortyardctl mcp` is a stdio shim for clients that only speak stdio. Both expose the same
tools.
acceptance: AC1: A remote agent with a URL and a token lists and calls tools with no local install.
AC2: Redirects are never followed with a token attached.
requirements.source: the prototype is stdio only (`clients/mcp_server.py`); legacy `cp_mcp.py` (HTTP, protocol versions 2025-03-26 to 2025-11-25).

requirements.title: Curated, role-scoped tools
requirements.statement:
Each role sees a small set of tools designed around what it does, at most 25 per role. Named
sets for 1.0: **worker** (`get_packet`, `submit_result`); **intake** (`file_tasks`,
`get_filing_verdict`, `search_tasks`, `get_task`, `add_note`); **groomer** (intake plus
`update_task`, `move_task`, `link_blocker`, `get_queue`); **sensor** (`file_finding`,
`search_findings`, `post_heartbeat`); **operator-agent** (`get_overview`, `get_attention`,
`get_queue`, `why_not_picked`, `get_task`, `get_chain`, `get_stage_outcomes`, `run_job`,
`requeue`, `cancel`, `resolve_hand_back`, `answer_decision`, `set_lanes`, `pause`, `resume`).
acceptance: AC1: `tools/list` returns exactly the tool set of the token's role: an `intake` token sees its five tools and nothing else; a worker token sees two (from MS3, MCP-005).
AC2: The tool list for each role is generated from role annotations on the OpenAPI operations and a curated manifest; a test fails if a manifest tool has no backing operation.

AC3: Demonstration (benchmark, MS5) — an operator-side agent with only an MCP address and a token performs the legacy operations inventory (BL-20): find why a task waits, requeue, cancel, run a job, resolve a hand-back, answer a decision, change lanes. Target: 100% of the inventory done with at most 25 tools in view, no cluster access and no shell. Floor: every operation the legacy scripts offer is done without cluster access or the shared board key (BL-20, BL-26).
requirements.source: PERMISSIONS.md "§7 rules"; legacy `cp_mcp.py` (a curated read-only set: `get_insights`, `get_overview`, `get_request`, `get_stage_outcomes`); the prototype exposes one tool per operation (194).
requirements.baseline: Agents operate the legacy system with the scripts of CLI-005, which need a shell in the cluster and the shared board key; its MCP server is read-only with four tools (driver §4 "Tools"; `cp_mcp.py`; BL-20, BL-26).

measured.target: 100% of the inventory done with at most 25 tools in view, no cluster access and no shell.
measured.floor: every operation the legacy scripts offer is done without cluster access or the shared board key (BL-20, BL-26).

requirements.title: Full reach through three generic tools
requirements.statement:
Every API operation the token may call is reachable through `list_operations`,
`describe_operation` and `call_operation`. This is how "APIs for everything, for agents" holds
without hundreds of tools.
acceptance: AC1: Parity test: for each role, the operations reachable through MCP equal the role's column of the permission matrix.
requirements.source: DESIGN §7; `clients/README.md` parity rule ("every API operation is exactly one MCP tool").

requirements.title: Bounded, honest tool results
requirements.statement:
Tool results are capped (default 48,000 characters) with a continuation cursor, say `unknown`
where the API returned null with a reason, and carry MCP annotations (`readOnlyHint`,
`destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`). A refusal from the API is passed back unchanged.
acceptance: AC1: A result over the cap is truncated at a record boundary and names how to continue.
requirements.source: `cp_mcp.py` (`MAX_RESULT_CHARS` 48,000; "A source reported unknown/unavailable is unknown, not zero").

requirements.title: Worker tools are the stage contract
requirements.statement:
A stage token can do two things: read its own packet and submit its own result. Both are
available as REST operations and as MCP tools.
acceptance: AC1: A stage token calling any other operation gets 403; calling another stage's packet gets 404.
requirements.source: DESIGN §7 ("a build worker can read its own context packet and submit its own stage result — nothing else").

requirements.title: `sortyardctl`
requirements.statement:
One CLI, installable with `pipx` and shipped in the image. Configuration: API URL and token from
environment, a profile file, or `--token-file`; a token is never accepted as an argument. Exit
codes: 0 success, 1 refused by the API, 2 usage, 3 unreachable.
acceptance: AC1: `sortyardctl --help` works offline and lists every command.
AC2: The process list never shows a token.
requirements.source: `clients/README.md` (`SORTYARD_API_URL`, `SORTYARD_TOKEN`, exit codes).

requirements.title: Commands for the things people and agents actually do
requirements.statement:
Task-level commands with readable output and `--json`: `task file|add|get|list|edit|move|note`,
`pickup status`, `queue`, `why`, `requeue`, `cancel`, `job run`, `decision list|answer`,
`needs list|discharge`, `lanes get|set`, `pause`, `resume`, `apply`, `export`, `audit`,
`health`, `backup`. Commands arrive with the capability they operate.
acceptance: AC1: Each command maps to exactly one documented sequence of API calls.
AC2: Human output and `--json` output are both covered by snapshot tests.
requirements.source: driver §4 "Tools", §7 "Common operations".

requirements.title: Every API operation is reachable
requirements.statement:
`sortyardctl api <operationId> [--param k=v] [--body JSON|@file|-]` calls any operation. A parity
test fails if an operation has no CLI path.
acceptance: AC1: Unknown operations or arguments send nothing.
requirements.source: `clients/README.md` parity rule; DESIGN §7 ("everything the CLI does is an API call (no back doors)").

requirements.title: Dry run
requirements.statement:
Mutating task-level commands accept `--dry-run` and print what would change, using the server's
own evaluation.
acceptance: AC1: `task file --dry-run` returns the verdict each task would get and writes nothing.
requirements.source: `drive.py --dry-run`, `plane_sync.py --dry-run`.

requirements.title: Parity with the legacy operator tools
acceptance: AC1: The migration guide has this table and each row has a test.

AC2: (WP5.11) Coverage of the legacy operations inventory (BL-20: the tools above, the legacy console's journeys and the steering done on the Plane board), as the share with a documented and tested Sortyard equivalent. Target: 100% by the MS5 gate. Floor: 100% of the operations the usage census (MIG-017) shows in use, before the first cutover.
requirements.source: driver §4 "Tools"; conductor README (tool descriptions).

measured.target: 100% by the MS5 gate.
measured.floor: 100% of the operations the usage census (MIG-017) shows in use, before the first cutover.

requirements.title: First-run bootstrap
requirements.statement:
A fresh install has no accounts and no default password. The chart creates a one-time setup
token in a Secret; presenting it once creates the first admin and invalidates the token.
acceptance: AC1: The API refuses every other operation until bootstrap completes.
AC2: The setup token cannot be used twice and expires (default after 24 hours); the docs say how to mint a new one.
requirements.source: inference — DESIGN §3.1 assumes an OIDC provider; a stranger's install has none. Plane benchmark: instance-admin first-run setup.

requirements.title: Operator sign-in
requirements.statement:
Three methods: local accounts (password hashed with argon2id, optional TOTP); OIDC; and a
trusted-proxy header mode for installations behind an authenticating proxy. Local accounts ship
in MS1; OIDC and the proxy mode are complete by MS6.
acceptance: AC1: A local account signs in with its password and, when enrolled, a TOTP code; a wrong second factor is refused and the attempt is audited.
AC2: (WP6.4) The proxy mode is refused at startup unless the API is unreachable except through the proxy (a NetworkPolicy the chart renders, verified by a startup probe).
AC3: (WP6.4) OIDC maps a claim to roles; a user with no mapping gets no access.

AC4: Demonstration (chaos, MS6) — a pod inside the cluster sends every mutating operation with a forged identity header, in each sign-in mode. Target: 100% refused and audited, in every mode. Floor: zero forged requests accepted; the legacy backend accepts them until it is locked down (BL-26).
requirements.source: harness-console decided D2, D16 (the `Tailscale-User-Login` header is forgeable from in-cluster pods until the backend is locked down); HC02-BACKEND-LOCKDOWN-DESIGN.
requirements.baseline: The legacy console trusts a `Tailscale-User-Login` header that pods inside the cluster can forge, and its mutation routes accept any same-network POST (harness-console decided D2, D16; VISION; BL-26).

measured.target: 100% refused and audited, in every mode.
measured.floor: zero forged requests accepted; the legacy backend accepts them until it is locked down (BL-26).

requirements.title: Session and request hardening
requirements.statement:
Cookie sessions are `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, with CSRF protection; mutations require
a same-origin request with a JSON body. Token-authenticated requests need no CSRF. The console
ships a strict Content-Security-Policy.
acceptance: AC1: A cross-site form post to any mutation is rejected.
AC2: A security-headers test runs against every route.
requirements.source: harness-console VISION ("mutation routes accept any same-network POST"), decided D2.

requirements.title: Human roles
requirements.statement:
`admin` (everything, including identity, credentials and integrations), `operator` (steer:
tasks, decisions, lanes, policies, requeue, cancel), `viewer` (read). A role binding is scoped
to the workspace or to one project.
acceptance: AC1: The permission matrix is generated from annotations in the OpenAPI document and published in the docs; a test fails if the page and the document disagree.
requirements.source: PERMISSIONS.md; DESIGN §3.9.

requirements.title: Service accounts and tokens
requirements.statement:
A service account has a role and a scope. Tokens are shown once, stored hashed, expire (default
90 days), can be revoked, and record last use. Issuing, rotating and revoking are audited.
acceptance: AC1: A database dump contains no usable token.
AC2: An expiring token is flagged in the token list ahead of expiry (default 14 days) and, from MS5, raises an attention item (OBS-014).
requirements.source: `identity/README.md` (scopes issued and revoked as data, every mutation audited); the owner's GitHub token expiry is tracked by hand today (driver §5).

requirements.title: Agent roles
requirements.statement:
Agent roles: `intake` (create tasks and notes in its project), `groomer` (intake plus edit,
order and link in its project), `sensor` (file findings and heartbeats in its project),
`operator-agent` (operator capabilities for unattended agents such as self-heal), and `worker`
(stage tokens only, IAM-007).
acceptance: AC1: Each role's allowed operations are a column of the matrix with an allow and a deny test per cell (IAM-010).
AC2: A sensor can search its own project's findings so that it can de-duplicate.
requirements.source: DESIGN §7; spec NOTES API ambiguity 5 ("a sensor therefore cannot de-duplicate against existing findings"); `SELF-HEAL.md` (an agent with host access works the queue).

requirements.title: Stage tokens
requirements.statement:
The controller mints one token per stage attempt, confined to that attempt and its chain epoch,
expiring at the stage deadline plus a margin, and revoked when the stage ends.
acceptance: AC1: A stage token used after its stage ended is refused.
requirements.source: `identity/README.md` ("a build-worker token, confined to one `stage_run_id`").

requirements.title: No agent can make its own work run
requirements.statement:
The invariant behind the design's "no token may create tasks and claim them": no principal
driven by a model can both introduce work and cause it to execute without passing gates it does
not control. Concretely: claiming is not grantable to anyone (API-017); a worker cannot create
tasks (follow-ups travel as stage output and are filed by the controller); tasks created by
agent principals are released only by the ready, preflight and release rules, which agents cannot
edit; system-created tasks record their origin and the rule that released them.
acceptance: AC1: No role's column contains both task creation and any release-rule or policy edit.
AC2: A worker-token call to create a task is refused.
AC3: The legacy pattern (the sync creates urgent triage items and the driver claims them, both deterministic) is allowed and attributed to `system:` actors.

AC4: Demonstration (count, MS1) — every credential is listed with whether it can introduce work and whether it can release or claim it, for the legacy system and for Sortyard. Target: zero credentials hold both, and 100% of the matrix cells are tested. Floor: fewer credentials hold both than in the legacy system, where one shared key does (BL-26).
requirements.source: DESIGN §7 (queue-poisoning vector); spec NOTES API ambiguity 6 (who creates `chain` and `eval-finding` tasks?); `plane_sync.queue_triage` and `drive` share one Plane key today.
requirements.baseline: The sync that files urgent triage items and the driver that claims them share one Plane key (DESIGN §7; `plane_sync.queue_triage`); by inference the filing tools use the same one (BL-26).

measured.target: zero credentials hold both, and 100% of the matrix cells are tested.
measured.floor: fewer credentials hold both than in the legacy system, where one shared key does (BL-26).

requirements.title: Authorisation is central, default-deny and object-scoped
requirements.statement:
One authorisation function decides every request from the operation's declared roles and the
caller's bindings. An operation with no declared role is unreachable. Object access is scoped in
the data-access layer: every query is constrained by the caller's workspace and project scope,
so an id from another scope behaves as not found.
acceptance: AC1: No handler contains its own role check (lint).
AC2: A request for an object outside the caller's scope returns 404, never 403 with details and never the object.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark — 57 of 89 published advisories are authorisation flaws (CWE-639, 862, 284, 863); see [12-quality-bar.md](12-quality-bar.md).

requirements.title: The authorisation matrix is tested cell by cell
requirements.statement:
For every operation × role there is an automated test asserting allow or deny, generated from
the matrix; and for every operation that takes an object id, a test that an id from another
project and another workspace is refused.
acceptance: AC1: Adding an operation without declaring its roles fails CI.
AC2: The generated suite runs on every PR in under two minutes.
requirements.source: `test_openapi.py` already checks the matrix document against the spec; this extends the check to the running service.

requirements.title: Audit log
requirements.statement:
Every mutation records actor, time, target, before and after (redacted), request id, client and
result, in an append-only store. A refused request is logged separately from mutations. The
audit trail of an object is visible on that object.
acceptance: AC1: The append-only guarantee is enforced by the database (update, delete and truncate refused), as in the existing migration.
AC2: The time from a mutating UI action to its entry in the entity's audit trail. Target: 1 s. Floor: 5 s.
requirements.source: harness-console J5 ("an audit entry (actor, time, target, result) is visible on the entity"); migration `0001` (refuse triggers).

requirements.title: Approval mode for agent-proposed actions
requirements.statement:
An operator-agent token, and the embedded concierge (UI-026), can run in approval mode: a
state-changing action becomes a proposal that a person approves, edits or rejects in the console
before it runs. The proposal shows the exact action and its effect; approving runs it as the
approver, audited with the proposer named.
acceptance: AC1: A proposal never executes without the approval of a person who holds the role the action needs; an edited proposal runs as edited.
AC2: The legacy journeys for approving and for editing an approval (J7, J12) pass against Sortyard.
AC3: A proposal is the stored "check" half of an action endpoint, which already separates check from do; no second execution path exists.
requirements.source: harness-console J7, decided D9; console e2e `j7-approve`, `j12-approval-edit`. Cut reversed on 2026-11-12: the feature is built and in the legacy console, and no measured case showed that removing it is better.

requirements.title: The console is a client of the public API
requirements.statement:
A single-page app served as static files by the API service. It uses only public API operations
and the event stream. There is no console-only endpoint.
acceptance: AC1: A test serves the console against a mock built from the OpenAPI document alone and every route renders.
AC2: A lint forbids request paths outside the generated API client.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 rule; SY-DEC-001 (Vite SPA, static files served by the API service).

requirements.title: UI-for-everything is measured
requirements.statement:
Operations are annotated `operator-facing` in the OpenAPI document. A coverage manifest maps
each to the route and control that invokes it. CI fails when an operator-facing operation has no
UI path, unless it carries a dated exemption.
acceptance: AC1: Coverage of operator-facing operations by a console control, from the manifest check. Target: 100% at every merge to `main`, with no exemption. Floor: 100% at each milestone exit for the operations introduced in that milestone or earlier.
AC2: The manifest is published as a docs page ("where is X in the UI").
requirements.source: Joe's objective ("there is a UI for everything"); CORPUS M5.6 defers every write surface to Phase 5 — see CF-03.

measured.target: 100% at every merge to `main`, with no exemption.
measured.floor: 100% at each milestone exit for the operations introduced in that milestone or earlier.

requirements.title: Board and list
requirements.statement:
The board shows tasks in columns by state; the list shows them in rows. Both support filters
(TRK-014), reordering of top-level tasks by drag or keyboard (TRK-007), and inline display of
park and hand-back reasons. Dragging changes rank only; state and priority are changed from the
item.
acceptance: AC1: Every drag has a keyboard equivalent and an undo.
AC2: The time from a drag to every open board and list showing the new order, without a reload. Target: 1 s. Floor: 5 s.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 1 ("Dragging is defined, not magic"); task-ready ("To reorder delivery, drag top-level tasks on the board").

requirements.title: Task detail is one timeline
requirements.statement:
One page per task: fields and spec, relations, the filing verdict and reasons, and one ordered
timeline of notes, state changes, decisions and — from MS3 — the chain: stages with attempts,
durations and outcomes, the change request, checks, review verdicts, usage. There is no separate
"pipeline" record to click through to.
acceptance: AC1: (WP3.9) From a task, the stage outcome that explains its current state is on the same page (zero navigation).
AC2: Every timeline entry has a stable deep link.

AC3: Demonstration (benchmark, MS3) — from a task, a scripted operator finds the stage outcome that explains its current state, on Sortyard and on the legacy pair. Target: zero navigation, shown within 1 s of opening the task. Floor: fewer steps than the legacy route across two tools (BL-18).
requirements.source: DESIGN §6.0 ("A task's detail *is* its chain"); Joe 2026-11-06 (the dashboard "connects tickets with the pipeline").
requirements.baseline: The ticket is in Plane and its runs are in the harness console: two tools with separate navigation (DESIGN §0; Joe 2026-11-06, the dashboard should connect "tickets with the pipeline"; BL-18).

measured.target: zero navigation, shown within 1 s of opening the task.
measured.floor: fewer steps than the legacy route across two tools (BL-18).

requirements.title: Creating and editing tasks
requirements.statement:
A form for the tracker fields and the typed spec with inline readiness feedback, a raw YAML view
of the same spec, and paste-or-upload of a task file with a per-task verdict preview before
filing.
acceptance: AC1: Form and YAML views round-trip without loss.
AC2: Readiness errors appear as the user types, from the server's evaluation.
requirements.source: task-ready "The task item"; `plane_tasks.py file`.

requirements.title: Pickup Preview and "why"
requirements.statement:
Per project: the queue in claim order, slot holders with phase and age, the reason code for
every task not claimable now, and the next-N simulation. On every task detail page: a "why is
this not running" panel with the same reasons and the tasks ranked ahead.
acceptance: AC1: Each reason code links to its documentation and, where an operator can fix it, to the control that does.
AC2: The view states the evaluation time and the policy versions it used.
requirements.source: task-pickup §7 (the "Where a reader sees it" column); HARNESS-251, HARNESS-256.

requirements.title: Owner list and decision inbox
requirements.statement:
One view of everything waiting on a person, grouped by route: decisions with their default and
time left, escalated premise-class decisions, needs routed to the viewer's route, items escalated
to a person. Decisions are answered here.
acceptance: AC1: Answering a decision records the chosen value and the route that will apply it.
AC2: A decision past its date that took its default shows as such, not as open.
requirements.source: driver §6 (the owner "answers `decision` items; defaults apply on their date"); conductor README (depends-on-Joe list, `needs-human`, `route:owner`).

requirements.title: Lanes and tuning
requirements.statement:
Edit lanes per project, pause and resume, admission caps and the scheduling policy values, with
the current value, the default, who last changed it and when. Saving shows the diff and its
effect on the Pickup Preview before it applies.
acceptance: AC1: A lane change needs no deploy and no file edit.
AC2: Every value shows the legacy constant it replaces where there is one (DEF-005).
requirements.source: driver §1 (knobs in `repos.yaml`, hardcoded copies in three files); DESIGN §5.3.

requirements.title: Overview: glance at the floor
requirements.statement:
The landing page: health state and what drives it; per project running, waiting, parked and
handed-back counts with oldest ages; slots and heavy-cap use; recent merges; the attention list.
It updates live.
acceptance: AC1: A source that is unknown or stale renders `unknown`, never 0.
AC2: Every number links to the list that produces it.
AC3: Render time of the Overview on the reference fixture. Target: 500 ms. Floor: 2 s, the legacy console's bar for the same journey.
requirements.source: harness-console J1; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN "Screen and feedback loop".

measured.floor: 2 s, the legacy console's bar for the same journey.

requirements.title: Chains and actions
requirements.statement:
For a chain: the stage timeline with attempts, durations, the reason a stage is waiting or
failed, and the binding. Actions — requeue, cancel, stop, resume — are offered only where the
API says they are legal, behind a dialog that states the effect; the result and its audit entry
appear inline.
acceptance: AC1: An action the API would refuse is not offered.
AC2: A run detail page never returns an error for an existing run; ids are unique.
requirements.source: harness-console J3, J5; VISION ("run detail currently 502s").

requirements.title: Logs and traces
acceptance: AC1: Opening a 5 MB log or trace. Target: first lines within 300 ms and no frame over 50 ms while scrolling. Floor: no frame over 200 ms (frame budget asserted in the e2e test).
requirements.source: harness-console J3; DESIGN §6 view 4.

measured.target: first lines within 300 ms and no frame over 50 ms while scrolling.
measured.floor: no frame over 200 ms (frame budget asserted in the e2e test).

requirements.title: Credentials
requirements.statement:
Accounts and keys with health, expiry and last use; add and re-authenticate through a stepper
that survives refresh and navigation, shows progress on slow steps, retries transient errors and
can be cancelled. Values are never shown and never entered except through the provider's own
flow or a paste-once field.
acceptance: AC1: Viewing the page triggers no paid probe.
AC2: A stuck flow can be cancelled for any provider.
requirements.source: harness-console J4; console routes `credentials`, components `add-account`, `sign-in`.

requirements.title: Parked and self-heal queues
requirements.statement:
Lists of parked and handed-back work with reason, blocking cause, age and what would bring each
back; the resolution actions of the self-heal contract (REC-009).
acceptance: AC1: Items older than the self-heal drain limit (default 24 h) are marked and match the `SELF-HEAL-STALLED` condition's list.
requirements.source: conductor README "Self-heal drain", "Blocking causes".

requirements.title: Health
acceptance: AC1: A silent mechanism is findable from the Overview in two clicks.
requirements.source: MECHANISMS.md; `GET /api/mh/factory/mechanisms`.

requirements.title: Dashboards
acceptance: AC1: Every tile's value matches a hand-computed fixture.
AC2: No dashboard requires Grafana or any service beyond Sortyard and Postgres.

AC3: A tile can show a reference series beside its own: a named baseline for the same metric and window, loaded through the API. The estate loads its legacy baselines this way (MIG-016), and the scorecard shows each criterion's floor and target as lines.
requirements.source: [09-observability.md](09-observability.md) metric catalogue; console route `delivery`, components `stage-timing`, `insights`.

requirements.title: Decision log and audit explorers
requirements.statement:
Search scheduling decisions by task, reason code, time and policy version, and open one
evaluation to see its inputs; browse the audit log by actor, object and time. A basic version
ships in MS2; saved searches and replay of an evaluation are complete by MS6.
acceptance: AC1: "Why was X not claimed at T" is answerable from the UI without the CLI.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 (DecisionLog explorer); harness-console `audit-trail` component.

requirements.title: Administration
requirements.statement:
Users, role bindings, service accounts and tokens; projects and repositories with an onboarding
wizard; system information (version, schema, image digest). Integrations, definitions and backup
controls join as their capabilities land; the page is complete at MS6 (WP6.4).
acceptance: AC1: A new project can be created and its first task filed without leaving the UI.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 12; onboarding.md (today: edit `repos.yaml`, push, wait for the onboarding check).

requirements.title: Performance budgets
requirements.statement:
The console keeps a normalised local store fed by the event stream, applies an operator's change
optimistically and reconciles with the server's answer, so that no action waits for a round trip
before it shows. Initial JavaScript is budgeted and enforced in CI. Grids are virtualised (about
50 rows mounted) and scroll 10,000 fixture rows smoothly. Lists use server cursors. Route code
is lazy-loaded and the next likely route is preloaded.
acceptance: AC1: Initial JavaScript, gzipped, enforced by the budget check. Target: 200 KB. Floor: 350 KB, the legacy console's budget.
AC2: An e2e test asserts the mounted-row bound on a 10,000-row fixture.

AC3: Interaction latency on the reference workload, from an input (click, key, end of a drag) to its visible result and from a route change to its content. Target: p95 at most 100 ms for an input and 200 ms for a route change. Floor: p95 at most 1 s, and no journey slower than on the legacy console (BL-18).
AC4: First load on a cold cache, to interactive, on the reference connection. Target: 1 s. Floor: 2 s.
AC5: An optimistic change that the server refuses is rolled back visibly, with the reason.
requirements.source: `console/check_budget.py` (`BUDGET_BYTES = 350 * 1024`); harness-console J2; decided D4. The local store and optimistic updates are a design change made on 2026-11-12 to reach the latency target (inference: a round trip for every action cannot meet it).

measured.floor: 350 KB, the legacy console's budget.

measured.target: p95 at most 100 ms for an input and 200 ms for a route change.
measured.floor: p95 at most 1 s, and no journey slower than on the legacy console (BL-18).

requirements.title: Accessibility
requirements.statement:
Target WCAG 2.2 AA. CI runs an automated accessibility scan on every route with zero serious or
critical violations, and every journey test is also run keyboard-only. Focus is managed on route
change and in dialogs; live updates are announced politely.
acceptance: AC1: The accessibility and keyboard specs are required checks.
AC2: Colour is never the only carrier of state.
requirements.source: harness-console journeys preamble ("keyboard-only, with zero serious/critical axe violations"); `console/e2e/tests/a11y.spec.ts`, `keyboard.spec.ts`; components `route-focus`, `announce`.

requirements.title: Responsive
requirements.statement: Every journey passes at 390, 834 and 1440 pixels wide.
acceptance: AC1: The e2e matrix runs the journeys at the three widths.
requirements.source: harness-console journeys preamble; VISION ("on a laptop or a phone").

requirements.title: Live without reload
requirements.statement:
Views update from the event stream, falling back to polling. A stale or disconnected view says
so.
acceptance: AC1: Killing the stream connection shows a "reconnecting" state and recovers without a reload.
requirements.source: harness-console J1; decided D5; console `lib/live.ts`.

requirements.title: Command palette
requirements.statement: A keyboard palette jumps to any task, chain or run by id or text and runs common actions.
acceptance: AC1: Typing `ROVE-12` and Enter opens that task from any page.
requirements.source: harness-console J2 ("⌘K palette jumps to any request/chain/run by id"); console `command-palette` component.

requirements.title: Design tokens and brand
requirements.statement: One token set (colour, type, spacing) with light and dark themes, using the Sortyard brand kit.
acceptance: AC1: No component hard-codes a colour.
requirements.source: meta-harness `projects/sortyard/branding/`; harness-console decided D3.

requirements.title: Empty, error and unknown states are designed
requirements.statement:
Every view has a designed state for: nothing yet, loading, failed to load, and value unknown.
An absent value is never rendered as zero, a blank or a spinner that never ends.
acceptance: AC1: Storybook (or equivalent) has a story per state per view, and the e2e suite visits the failed and unknown states.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "Testing model" (one story per machine state; every gate defines its absent state); harness-console J1.

requirements.title: Strings are externalised; English only
requirements.statement:
All user-visible strings go through a message catalogue with locale-aware dates and numbers.
1.0 ships English only and documents how a locale is added.
acceptance: AC1: A lint fails on a hard-coded user-visible string in a component.
AC2: A pseudo-locale build renders every route without clipped or missing text.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (22 locales, an i18n sync check in CI); see [12-quality-bar.md](12-quality-bar.md) for the stance.

requirements.title: Embedded concierge
requirements.statement:
The console keeps the embedded concierge of the existing console: ask a question, get an answer
grounded in live state with citations, and approve proposed actions (IAM-012). It is a client of
the operator-agent tools (MCP-002) with the signed-in operator's permissions, it has no private
endpoint, and it is off until a model credential is configured for it. Its ambient half, the
attention list, ships in MS5 (OBS-014).
acceptance: AC1: The legacy concierge journeys (J6, and the second concierge journey of J12) pass against Sortyard.
AC2: Every statement the concierge makes about state cites the record it came from; text from tasks, logs and traces is treated as data, never as instructions.
AC3: With no model credential the entry point says how to enable it, and nothing else in the console changes.
AC4: Time to the first token of an answer on the reference workload. Target: 1 s. Floor: no slower than the legacy concierge (BL-18).
requirements.source: harness-console J6–J8, decided D7–D9, D14–D15; console `components/concierge/*`, `concierge.py`; e2e `j6-concierge`, `j12-concierge-2`. Cut reversed on 2026-11-12: the feature is built and shipped in the legacy console, and no measured case showed that removing it is better; how much it is used is counted by the census (MIG-017). Owner decision OD-3.

measured.floor: no slower than the legacy concierge (BL-18).

requirements.title: One ordered ledger, written with the state it describes
requirements.statement:
Every state change writes one event `{seq, time, actor, object, transition, facts, refs}` in the
same database transaction as the change. Events are append-only and globally ordered by `seq`.
Scheduling decisions and audit entries are event classes in the same order, so one task's
timeline interleaves all three.
acceptance: AC1: There is no code path that changes a state table without an event (enforced by routing all writes through domain commands and a test that diffs tables against events after the scenario suite).
AC2: Appending the same event twice records it once; reusing an id for different content is refused.
AC3: Update, delete and truncate on ledger tables are refused by the database.

AC4: Demonstration (count, MS7) — the stores that hold delivery state or history are counted for the legacy system and for the pilot installation, and the pilot's tables are diffed against its events. Target: one store, and zero state changes without an event over the whole pilot. Floor: fewer stores than the legacy inventory, and zero unexplained differences between tables and events (BL-14, BL-24).
requirements.source: migration `0001` (append-only triggers, `append_event` idempotency); DESIGN §3.8; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN ("A durable event ledger is the follow-up for exact historical series").
requirements.baseline: State and history are spread over `state.json`, `grooming.json`, the dispatcher's SQLite database, JSONL ledgers and the board's database, with no common order; they have disagreed in production (HARNESS-256; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN; BL-14, BL-24).

measured.target: one store, and zero state changes without an event over the whole pilot.
measured.floor: fewer stores than the legacy inventory, and zero unexplained differences between tables and events (BL-14, BL-24).

requirements.title: History of any object
requirements.statement: For any object the API returns its events in order, with who, when, before and after.
acceptance: AC1: The current state of a task equals the fold of its events (replay test).
requirements.source: `sortyard.object_history(kind, id)`; harness-console J5.

requirements.title: Read models are projections and say so
requirements.statement:
Aggregates (queue census, throughput windows, dashboards) are computed from the ledger and
state tables, are recomputable at will, store nothing authoritative, and are labelled with
`as_of`. A read model never feeds a scheduling decision.
acceptance: AC1: Dropping and rebuilding every read model changes no API result other than `as_of`.
AC2: A read endpoint causes no write, no Job and no outbound call.
requirements.source: FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN ("The read model is a projection of source records, never a second authority"; "No request body, database write, Job creation, or trace span is caused by these reads").

requirements.title: The metric catalogue
requirements.statement:
Sortyard ships one catalogue in which each metric has an id, an exact definition (numerator,
denominator, clock, window, cohort), a unit and its coverage rule. The v1 catalogue:

| Id | Definition |
|---|---|
| `queue.actionable` | Eligible tasks and admissible stages now, by project and state. Age runs from the release or queued transition to first schedule; open waits use `as_of`. |
| `stage.pickup_latency` | For stages first scheduled in the window: `first_scheduled − eligible_since`, where `eligible_since` is the later of the queued transition and the predecessor's pass. Dependency wait is reported separately and is never called a scheduler delay. |
| `stage.execution` | For attempts terminal in the window: scheduled→running, running→collecting, collecting→terminal. Missing endpoints are counted, not dropped. |
| `chain.outcomes` | Chains that reached a terminal outcome in the window, once each, by outcome (done, parked, handed-back, cancelled), with shares. |
| `chain.cycle_time` | For chains done in the window: done − claimed. Open chains are shown by current age, not included in percentiles. |
| `task.lead_time` | For tasks done in the window: done − created; and time in each board state. |
| `merges` | Change requests merged into a default branch in the window, by host merge time, unique by repo and number. |
| `merge.open_to_first_green` / `merge.green_to_merge` / `merge.open_to_merge` | From the change request's history and its required check runs. |
| `review.rounds` | Reviews with a verdict per task; share of tasks at or over the tripwire. |
| `fix.rounds`, `conflict.rounds` | Per task and per window. |
| `lanes.utilisation` | Slot-seconds held ÷ slot-seconds available, by project; same for each heavy cap. |
| `handback.count`, `park.count` | By reason and blocking-cause kind. |
| `cost.agent_minutes_per_merge` | Agent wall time of every finished stage for a project (builds, reviews, fix rounds, triage, failures) ÷ changes merged in its repos, same window. |
| `cost.stages_per_merge`, `cost.tokens_per_merge` | Same cohort; tokens where recorded. |
| `main.health` | Per repo: latest completed required run on the default branch, its conclusion, and the age of the last success. |
| `chain.control_wait` | For chains terminal in the window: the sum of the gaps between an enabling event and the action it enables (stage finished → next dispatched, checks green → merge armed, verdict → next round, merge observed → Done). Excludes time in agents, CI, reviews and waiting for a slot (FLW-019). |
| `stall.episodes` | Episodes in the window in which a chain passed a phase bound or a stage made no progress: count, share recovered with no person, time to detection, time to recovery (REC-026). |
| `operator.interventions` | Mutations by a person on work in flight (requeue, cancel, force, manual state change, resolving a hand-back), for each week and for each 100 merged tasks; owner-list answers are counted separately (REC-024). |
| `upgrade.impact` | For each upgrade: failed API requests, missed events, time without a leader, stages failed or retried because of it (DEP-010). |
acceptance: AC1: Each metric has a fixture with a hand-computed expected value.
AC2: A metric whose source is incomplete returns `null` with a reason (API-012).
AC3: Percentiles use nearest-rank and state `n`.

AC4: The four comparison metrics (`chain.control_wait`, `stall.episodes`, `operator.interventions`, `upgrade.impact`) have one definition each, shared by the tests that record them from MS3 on and by the catalogue, so a demonstration and a dashboard cannot disagree.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract "Metric definitions"; `metrics/analyze.py` (merged per day, open→first green, last green→merge, open→merge, review rounds, auto-merge use); conductor README `cost_item`.

requirements.title: Throughput windows
requirements.statement:
Catalogue metrics are available per hour, day and week, by project, lane and workflow. Windows
describe the past and gate nothing.
acceptance: AC1: Window boundaries are half-open and in UTC; a record is counted in exactly one window.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.8 ThroughputWindow; Joe 2026-11-05 (time survives only as looking back at throughput).

requirements.title: Delivery cost
requirements.statement:
For each project and window: agent-minutes per merged change and stages per merged change,
computed from recorded stage usage. Stages whose usage is unreadable are named, not guessed.
acceptance: AC1: The published number and the list of excluded stages always appear together.

AC2: Demonstration (ledger, MS7) — agent-minutes and stages for each merged change over the pilot's window, from the ledger, against the same project's legacy figure. Target: no agent-minute is spent on a stage that could not succeed (missing base, unregistered target, unreadable input), and the figure is available for any window and project within 1 s. Floor: cost for each merged change no higher than the legacy baseline, and the figure kept as a series for any past window, which the legacy item cannot give (BL-16).
requirements.source: driver §3 "Delivery cost" (k3s-harness #186: "Unreadable requests are named, not guessed").
requirements.baseline: The sync writes a delivery-cost item on each board for the current window; the cost of a merged change is not kept as a series (conductor README `cost_item`; k3s-harness #186; BL-16).

measured.target: no agent-minute is spent on a stage that could not succeed (missing base, unregistered target, unreadable input), and the figure is available for any window and project within 1 s.
measured.floor: cost for each merged change no higher than the legacy baseline, and the figure kept as a series for any past window, which the legacy item cannot give (BL-16).

requirements.title: Wait versus work
requirements.statement:
For any chain and any window the time is decomposed into: waiting on dependencies, waiting for a
slot, waiting for admission, executing, waiting on CI, waiting on review, waiting on a person.
acceptance: AC1: The components sum to the cycle time within one second.
AC2: Each component maps to reason codes (SCH-009), so the dashboard and the Pickup Preview agree.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract ("Stage timing waterfall and wait-vs-execution decomposition"); FACTORY-STAGE-ATTEMPTS-DESIGN.

requirements.title: Queue census
requirements.statement:
A cheap, bounded endpoint returns current counts: eligible, held by reason, claimed by phase,
stages queued, running and collecting, slots and caps in use. Downstream stages of an open chain
are future work, not queue depth.
acceptance: AC1: The census never counts a stage under a terminal chain as runnable.
requirements.source: `GET /api/mh/queue-census`; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN (`eligible_queued_stages` rule).

requirements.title: Daily record
requirements.statement:
One generated record per day and project: what merged, what did not and why, what is parked or
handed back, incidents on main, quarantined jobs, cost. Generated from the ledger; nobody writes
it by hand.
acceptance: AC1: The record for a past day is reproducible byte for byte.

AC2: Demonstration (ledger, MS6) — the daily record is generated twice for 14 past days of the reference workload. Target: byte-identical on every re-run, ready within 60 s of the day's end, with zero model calls. Floor: every figure of the legacy report is present and reproducible, and no agent run is spent writing it (BL-27).
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 13 ("no hand-written status ever again"); JOB-QUARANTINE.md (`ledger/pipeline-daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md`).
requirements.baseline: Throughput reports and Slack cards are written by an agent on a schedule, and the daily pipeline record is a file committed to a repository (driver §6; JOB-QUARANTINE.md; BL-27).

measured.target: byte-identical on every re-run, ready within 60 s of the day's end, with zero model calls.
measured.floor: every figure of the legacy report is present and reproducible, and no agent run is spent writing it (BL-27).

requirements.title: System metrics endpoint
requirements.statement:
Each component serves Prometheus metrics: reconcile duration and lag, claim latency, queue
